keywords: 怎么追踪策略中间变量
title: Trace intermediate variables in realize()
summary: Use self.trace(name, var) under trace_log to record scalars while realize() runs. Tracing is not a run mode. FactorSorter and GeneralStg are not adapted yet.
narrative:
Tracing records intermediate values while a strategy's realize() runs so you can inspect them after a backtest.

Call self.trace(name, var) inside realize(). Only int, float, bool, and str (including matching numpy scalars) are accepted—lists and arrays raise TypeError. Enable via QT_CONFIG['trace_log'] (default True); the backtester calls Operator.enable_tracing(). When tracing is off, trace() is a silent no-op.

Column names look like {strategy_id}_{variable}. Read results from Strategy.get_trace_data() or Backtester.trace_result_df after a run.

Limits: FactorSorter and GeneralStg are not adapted yet (vector returns versus scalar trace). Tracing is not a run mode—do not use mode=3 (forecast stats) or mode=4 (invalid) as a "trace mode"; use trace_log.

How to declare Parameter / get_data belongs to the realize card.
python_code:
import qteasy as qt
op = qt.Operator(strategies='dma', signal_type='pt')
stg = op.strategies[0]
stg.enable_tracing(max_steps=3)
for i in range(3):
    stg.update_trace_step(i)
    stg.trace('note', f'step-{i}')
print(stg.get_trace_data())
risk_notes: Tracing adds memory. Empty tables usually mean trace_log is off or FactorSorter/GeneralStg was used.
